profile.headline: Machine learning for audio and biosignals.
profile.summary:
Researcher specializing in audio event detection and audio scene recognition. Industry experience building CNN and transformer models, audio event detection, fitness tracking, wearables, signal processing, and instrumentation. Doctoral training in auditory processing, neurophysiology, and machine learning.

Specialties:
Machine learning, audio signal recognition, transformer models for audio, biosignal analysis, auditory processing, computational neuroscience, bioinformatics, data analysis, laboratory instrumentation.

positions.title: Software Engineer, Sound Understanding Group
positions.description: Investigating audio and multimodal generation, editing, and analysis.

positions.title: Software Engineer, Sound Understanding group
positions.description: Built AudioSet, the standard dataset for audio event detection. Transferred research to products including YouTube, Pixel Buds, and Nest. Researched machine learning methods for audio and multimodal signals.

positions.title: Senior Algorithms Research Engineer
positions.description: Calorimetry and fitness algorithms for the Apple Watch.

positions.title: Senior Scientist for Algorithms and Signal Processing
positions.description: Led development and implementation of algorithms and signal processing for IPC's optical sensors and medical devices. Invented and implemented the detection algorithm at the core of IPC's point-of-care diagnostics insrtument. Techniques included linear systems analysis in a high-dimensionality dense-coding regime, characterization of noise levels and corelation, maximum-likelihood and MAP parameter estimation, and nonlinear classification in a compressed sensing regime.

positions.title: Image Processing Consultant
positions.description: Implemented a state-of-the-art text detection algorithm and integrated it into IQ Engines' computer vision pipeline. Researched possible algorithms, prototyped and compared accuracy and speed using Python, and accelerated using C.

positions.title: Graduate Student Researcher
positions.description:
Working with my advisor Fréderic Theunissen, I designed and executed several animal experiments to probe the neural and computational mechanisms of auditory processing. I made single-unit extracellular recordings from Zebra Finches, a major model system for auditory research, and analyzed the results using state-of-the-art machine learning and data handling techniques.

In one of these experiments, I discovered a class of neurons in auditory forebrain that is highly resistant to corruption by background noise. This work was published in PLOS Computational Biology in 2013, and our presentation of preliminary results at the annual Society for Neuroscience meeting in late 2010 garnered coverage on NPR's All Things Considered.

Using the understanding of auditory computation, I am working with another student in the lab to construct a real-time noise-rejection algorithm for human speech.

positions.description: Adapted a novel sub-wavelength-resolution surface-plasmon optical technology for photolithography. This work was ultimately published in PNAS.

positions.title: Project Manager
positions.description: Lead development, transfer to manufacturing, and support of the COPAS Plus, COPAS Select, and COPAS XL flow cytometers. Developed large-bore flowcells and fluidic controls, and generated IP to support the products and reagents.

positions.title: Research Engineer
positions.description: Developed fluidic systems and designed mechanical parts as part of the R&D team for the COPAS Biosort flow cytometer. Supported product on early installations and helped train field service team.
